2] Heard.

3] This petition has been filed by the petitioners under A 227 of the Constitution of India against the order dated 11.12.2023, passed in Case No.MACC 271/2022 by the MACT, Mandsaur, whereby, the documents submitted by the petitioners in evidence have been returned holding the same to be not relevant.

4] In brief, the facts of the case are that the petitioners have filed the aforesaid claim case on account of death of Jitendra Singh, the son of the petitioner Nos.1 and 2, and brother of petitioner Nos.3 and 4 whereas, and grandson of petitioner No.5.
The case of the petitioner is that Jitendra was studying in GSITS, Indore and was a final year student of B.E., who met with an accident on 09.05.2022, in which he and his friend died.

Subsequently, a claim case was filed as aforesaid, in which, initially an application under Section 169 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was filed, which was allowed by the Claims Tribunal vide order dated 17.10.2023 as the petitioners wanted to bring certain certificates of Jitendra and his friends on record.

However, subsequently, vide impugned order dated 11.12.2023,
at the time of recording of the evidence, although the documents relating to the petitioner Nos.1 and Raghuveer Singh vs Manoj Patel on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140762280/
2 2's son have been allowed to be taken on record, however, the documents which related to their son's friend have not been allowed to be exhibited and have been returned to the petitioners stating that these documents are not relevant.
5] Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the aforesaid documents which related to the friends of the deceased Jitendra were relevant to demonstrate that had Jitendra been alive, he would also have earned in the same fashion in which his friends who were similarly qualified, were earning.

Thus, it is submitted that the petitioners were entitled to draw a parity with the career opportunities which the petitioner Nos.1 and 2's son would have availed in the same manner in which his friends have availed, and which he and they missed out on account of his death.
Thus, it is submitted that the application ought to have been allowed.

6] In support of his submissions, counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the decision rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of M.R .Krishna Murthi Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and Others reported as (2020) 15 SCC 493, para 25.

sentences.text: 7] None appeared for the respondents despite of service of notice.
8] Heard.

On due consideration of submissions and on perusal of the documents filed on record, it is apparent that the petitioner Nos.1 and 2' son, who was a bright student pursuing his B.E. final year from GSITS, Indore, but has unfortunately died in a fatal accident.

It is also found that earlier, the petitioners' application to bring the documents relating to their son and his friends was allowed vide order dated 17.10.2023, however, some of those documents have been returned on the ground that they are not relevant and relates to the deceased's friends.

9] On perusal of the aforesaid documents which the petitioners wanted to place on record, this Court finds that the aforesaid documents are the documents relating to the petitioner Nos.1 and 2's son's friends and their earnings, as the petitioners wanted to draw a parity with the income earned by the friends of the deceased.

10] In the considered opinion of this Court, the aforesaid parity which the petitioners wanted to draw, was perfectly in accordance with law, as they were entitled to bring on record and to prove in evidence, such documents, which could improve their chances of proper and just compensation, and in such circumstances, the impugned order cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.

11] Accordingly,
the petition stands allowed, the impugned order dated 11.12.2023 is hereby set aside, and the learned Member of the Claims Tribunal is requested to allow the petitioners to place on record all such documents, through which they want to draw parity with their son's future income. 12] With the aforesaid, the petition stands allowed and disposed of.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Bahar Raghuveer Singh vs Manoj Patel on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140762280/
